newsitem.title: USA: Viacom Q1 revenues grew across the board.
newsitem.headline: Viacom Q1 revenues grew across the board.

text.p: Media behemoth Viacom Inc Wednesday reported first quarter revenue growth in every business segment and a smaller-than-expected loss for the period.

The company reported $2.9 billion in total revenues, $392 million in EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization), and operating income of $174 million for the quarter. A year ago Viacom posted revenues of $2.6 billion, EBITDA of $448 million, and operating income of $256 million.
The company said the revenue growth was led by double-digit gains at MTV Networks, Blockbuster Video, and its Paramount motion picture and television operations.

Viacom said revenue and EBITDA comparisons were affected by benefits realized in the first quarter of 1996 from programming licenses related to the alliance with KirchGroup, the German media group. Those benefits more than offset benefits realized in the first quarter of 1997 from programming licenses related to the alliance with Television Par Satellite.
Excluding the impact of these alliances, Viacom's EBITDA for the latest quarter increased 4 percent or $15 million.
For the first quarter, Viacom reported a net loss from continuing operations of $24 million, or $0.11 per share.
This compared to earnings from continuing operations of $19 million, or $0.01 per share, in 1996's first quarter.
The First Call consensus estimate for the latest quarter was a loss of $0.16 per share.

Reflecting a profit from discontinued operations for the first three months of 1997, Viacom reported a net loss of $18.7 million and a loss attributable to common stock of $34 million, or $0.10 per share, versus net earnings of $27.8 million, or $.03 per share, in 1996.

"Viacom's 1997 first quarter results were led by the strong performance of our Networks and Broadcasting segment, particularly MTV Networks, which had revenue and EBITDA increases of 15 percent and 23 percent, respectively," chief executive Sumner Redstone said.
The company said total Networks and Broadcasting revenues increased 11 percent to $577 million and EBITDA increased 17 percent to $160 million.

"Our Entertainment segment also made substantial contributions in the period, while our seasonally driven Publishing and our Video and Music/Parks segments remain on track for improved performance in the second half of 1997," Redstone said.
The company reported "equity in loss of affiliated companies, net of tax" of $15 million for the first quarter of 1997 versus earnings, net of tax, of $1 million for the same prior-year period.
It said the decrease resulted principally from losses at United Paramount Network, 50 percent of which was acquired by Viacom on January 15.
